Definition: from G303 and G4579; figuratively, to excite:--move, stir up.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to stir up, to excite: the chief priests moved the people to ask for Barabbas instead of Jesus, and the accusers said Jesus stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place. It is the stirring of a crowd — the priests moving the people one way, and the charge that Jesus moved them the other.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for stirring up carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the crowd — moved by the chief priests to choose Barabbas, and charged with being stirred up by Jesus.
